title: Compare and Contrast Transmission Media and Transceivers

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Network data travels over wireless, copper, or fiber media. The equipment at both ends must support compatible standards, speeds, transceivers, and connectors.
bullets: Wired: 802.3, fiber, DAC/twinax, coax, cable speeds, and plenum ratings
Fiber, telephone, Ethernet, and coax connector types
sections.callout: Medium → standard → speed and distance → transceiver → connector.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a scenario describes distance, environment, cable, connector, wireless technology, or transceiver requirements, can you identify the appropriate transmission technology?
bullets: Threaded coax → F-type; bayonet coax → BNC

entries.title: 802.11 Standards
paragraphs: The IEEE 802.11 family defines wireless LAN technology commonly called Wi-Fi. Versions differ by frequency, speed, channels, and performance.
entries.recognitionCue: A wireless LAN standard is required → 802.11.

entries.title: Cellular
paragraphs: Cellular networks use a carrier's infrastructure for phones, tablets, hotspots, mobile Internet, and WAN backup.
entries.recognitionCue: A mobile or backup connection uses a carrier network → Cellular.

entries.title: Satellite
paragraphs: Satellite provides broad geographic coverage where terrestrial broadband may be unavailable, though latency depends on the satellite architecture.
entries.recognitionCue: A rural site has no cable or fiber service → Satellite.

entries.title: 802.3 Standards
paragraphs: The IEEE 802.3 family defines Ethernet standards over copper and fiber.
entries.recognitionCue: A wired LAN standard is required → 802.3.

entries.title: Single-Mode Fiber
paragraphs: Single-mode fiber uses a small core and is designed for longer-distance, high-bandwidth links such as backbones, WANs, and provider connections.

entries.title: Multimode Fiber
paragraphs: Multimode fiber uses a larger core with multiple light paths and is commonly used for shorter links in buildings, campuses, and data centers.

entries.title: Direct Attach Copper (DAC) Cable
paragraphs: DAC is a short, high-speed copper cable assembly commonly used between nearby switches and servers. Its transceiver ends are generally integrated.

entries.title: Twinaxial Cable
paragraphs: Twinaxial cable has two inner conductors and is commonly the medium used in DAC assemblies.

entries.title: Coaxial Cable
paragraphs: Coaxial cable has a central conductor, insulation, and shielding. It is associated with cable broadband and legacy network uses.

entries.title: Cable Speeds
paragraphs: The medium must support the required bandwidth, distance, network standard, and equipment interface. A faster switch port cannot exceed the capability of an incompatible cable or transceiver.
entries.memoryHook: The cable must support the link.

entries.title: Plenum vs. Non-Plenum Cable
paragraphs: Plenum-rated cable is designed for air-handling spaces where fire and smoke characteristics matter. Non-plenum cable is used only where building codes and installation requirements permit it.

sections.title: Transceivers
paragraphs: A transceiver transmits and receives. Modular transceivers allow interfaces to support different media, speeds, distances, and protocols.

entries.title: Ethernet
paragraphs: An Ethernet transceiver carries general network traffic and must match the equipment, medium, speed, and interface.

entries.title: Fibre Channel (FC)
paragraphs: Fibre Channel is strongly associated with high-speed storage and SAN traffic; it is not simply another name for Ethernet over fiber.

entries.title: Small Form-Factor Pluggable (SFP)
paragraphs: SFP is a modular transceiver form factor available for different media and link capabilities.

entries.title: Quad Small Form-Factor Pluggable (QSFP)
paragraphs: QSFP is a high-capacity modular transceiver family. SFP and QSFP are form factors, not cable connector types.

entries.title: 802.11 vs. 802.3
paragraphs: 802.11 is wireless LAN. 802.3 is Ethernet.

entries.title: Single-Mode vs. Multimode
paragraphs: Single-mode supports longer distance; multimode is associated with shorter links.

entries.title: SFP/QSFP vs. SC/LC
paragraphs: SFP and QSFP are transceiver form factors. SC, LC, ST, and MPO are fiber connector types.

entries.title: RJ11 vs. RJ45
paragraphs: RJ11 is associated with telephone wiring. RJ45 is associated with twisted-pair Ethernet.

entries.title: F-Type vs. BNC
paragraphs: Both use coax. F-type has a strong cable/broadband association; BNC uses a bayonet lock.
